labels.label: [8.G] (l.2307-2309, l.2320-2326): the contracting graph and its achronality; the null-line Cauchy criterion for entire strictly contracting graphs (design §1A-B)

hypotheses.paper: S~ is the developed complete spacelike hypersurface
hypotheses.note: an arbitrary entire strictly contracting graph; that S~ is one is bprop:project (CauchyComplete)
strict reading IsStrictContraction (= acausal graph); 1-Lipschitz where it suffices

findings: The exact Cauchy criterion for an entire strictly contracting graph of M^n is 'meets every null affine line' (isCauchySurface_graph_iff, both directions closed); timelike lines are met automatically (existsUnique_mem_graph_line). It sharpens Achronal's SCOPE remark that a uniform kappa < 1 is sufficient, not necessary. What it says about l.2491 is recorded under the separate bprop:danom entry.

labels.label: bprop:danom, l.2489-2491 'every nonspacelike line of M meets D(S~ x {t})' (W7; false as written)

hypotheses.paper: D(S~ x {t}) the developed slice (D = developing map)
hypotheses.note: an arbitrary entire strictly contracting graph of M^n; no developing map, no quotient

findings: By isCauchySurface_graph_iff, l.2491's claim, for a strictly contracting entire graph (here the developed slice D(S~ x {t}), D the developing map), says exactly that the slice is a Cauchy surface of M^n. The hyperboloid (Rem 2.2) is a strictly contracting entire graph whose domain of dependence is only the open future cone (dependenceDomain_hyperboloid) and which is no Cauchy surface of M^n (not_isCauchySurface_graph_hyperboloid): the claim fails for it. This confirms docs/BARBOT-WAVE3.md §0 W7 (in the hyperboloid quotient, null lines through the vertex miss every slice) and is why the design repairs bprop:danom without slices. Barbot does not use a Cauchy criterion at l.2491; he asserts the meeting property, which is what fails.

labels.label: Rem 2.2 (the hyperboloid, standard example)

hypotheses.note: 0 < d (n >= 2) for dependenceDomain_hyperboloid and isOpen_dependenceDomain_hyperboloid, where it is needed (for d = 0 the hyperboloid is the point t = 1 and D is the whole line; Achronal's isCauchySurface_graph_hyperboloid_zero), and for isCauchySurfaceOn_futureCone_hyperboloid, where it is NOT needed (for d = 0, Omega = {t > 0} and S = {t = 1} is still Cauchy for Omega) but inherited from the proof route through D(S) (now sorry-free); the d = 0 case is now stated and proved separately as isCauchySurfaceOn_futureCone_hyperboloid_zero (through isCauchySurfaceOn_graph_of_saturated with W = Omega = {t > 0}; the line-meeting hypothesis from Achronal's isCauchySurface_graph_hyperboloid_zero), so Rem 2.2's first half holds for every n for the future component
only the future component {t > |x|}; the past one (graph of -hyperboloid, Achronal's graph_neg_hyperboloid) follows by time reflection and is not stated (disclosed in SCOPE)

findings: The hyperboloid misses many null lines, not only those through the vertex: the null line r + s l (l != 0, Q(l) = 0) meets it iff l.1 * <r|l> < 0 (exists_mem_graph_hyperboloid_null_iff, closed); for l = (1, e), |e| = 1, iff <r.2, e> < r.1, i.e. iff the line enters the open future cone {t > |x|} = D(S) (exists_mem_graph_hyperboloid_null_iff_isFutureTimelike, closed). E.g. (-1, 0) + s(1, e) misses it without passing through 0. The null lines through the vertex are the boundary case <r|l> = 0 (exists_nullLine_not_mem_graph_hyperboloid proves one of them). Its domain of dependence in M^n is exactly the open future cone {Q < 0, t > 0} (dependenceDomain_hyperboloid, closed): Rem 2.2's Omega is D(S).

The hyperboloid satisfies (CC') (ccPrime_graph_hyperboloid, closed: on a null hyperplane <r|l> is constant, so either all or none of its l-lines meet S), although it is no Cauchy surface of M^n: (CC') is Cauchy-completeness, consistent with Rem 2.2's 'Omega is MGH'.

labels.label: design §1C: causal convexity, hub lemma, (CC') transfer

hypotheses.paper: design: lgraph f ⊆ W and 0 <= T z in the hub lemma
hypotheses.note: not needed (T z < 0 makes the set empty)
only the causal core the design assigns here (causal convexity, hub compactness, (CC') transfer), all closed without sorry; bprop:ghyp itself is not claimed

findings: W8's obligation (components causally convex) has a general form: any open W ⊆ M^n with an acausal Cauchy surface is causally convex, segments included (segment_subset_of_isCauchySurfaceOn). Prop 8.12 (step 3, Sigma Cauchy in Omega' = range D) can cite it. Prop 8.10 / W8 cannot without circularity (causal convexity of the components of int U(Gamma) is an input to their global hyperbolicity, so no Cauchy surface is yet available); there convexity of the components already gives the segment form.
CCPrime is inhabited (kb/0011): ccPrime_graph_const (horizontal hyperplanes) and ccPrime_graph_hyperboloid.

labels.label: design §1D: domain of dependence

hypotheses.note: interior used throughout (design's fallback); openness proved for the hyperboloid

findings: D(S) of a strictly contracting entire graph is exactly the set of points every causal affine line through which meets S (meets_of_mem_dependenceDomain / mem_dependenceDomain_of_meets); D(S) and int D(S) are closed under J^- inside {T >= 0} and under J^+ inside {T <= 0}. S is a Cauchy surface of int D(S) with no sorry (isCauchySurfaceOn_interior_dependenceDomain), so Rem 2.2's first half isCauchySurfaceOn_futureCone_hyperboloid is now sorry-free too.

The Cauchy argument uses only three properties of the open set W: every causal affine line through a point of W meets S, and W is closed under J^- inside {T >= 0} and under J^+ inside {T <= 0}. It is stated for any such W (isCauchySurfaceOn_graph_of_saturated); int D(S) is one instance (isCauchySurfaceOn_interior_dependenceDomain, now a corollary), the d = 0 future cone {t > 0} another (isCauchySurfaceOn_futureCone_hyperboloid_zero).

kb_proposals: Time reflection (t,x) -> (-t,x) with f -> -f turns every past-side statement about graphs into the future one by pure algebra on points (le flips, T_{-f}(refl p) = -T_f(p)); state the past lemma for functions g : R -> M^n with the explicit cone inequality rather than for causal curves, so the reflected function satisfies it without transporting inextensibility.

A causal affine line of M^n is an inextensible causal curve over R once parametrised by time (timeLine p v, inextensible_timeLine); its components in an open W (inextensible_ordConnectedComponent) are the way to use IsCauchySurfaceOn W.
